title: Why you remember embarrassing moments forever
description:
You forgot what you ate last Tuesday, but you will never forget that one awkward sentence. Psychologists call part of this negativity bias: bad events tend to weigh more than good ones, and emotional moments are stored more strongly in memory.

Sources: Baumeister et al., 2001, Review of General Psychology ("Bad is stronger than good"); McGaugh, 2004, Annual Review of Neuroscience ("The amygdala modulates the consolidation of memories of emotionally arousing experiences").

#shorts #psychology #memory

scenes.headline: LAST TUESDAY?
scenes.text: You forgot what you ate last Tuesday, but you'll never forget that one awkward sentence.

scenes.headline: WHY FOREVER?
scenes.text: Why do embarrassing moments last forever?

scenes.headline: NEGATIVITY BIAS
scenes.text: Psychologists have a name for it: negativity bias.

scenes.headline: WHAT STICKS
scenes.text: In a famous review, researchers found that bad events tend to have a stronger effect on us than good ones.

scenes.headline: STAMPED IN
scenes.label: MEMORY
scenes.text: And emotional moments get stamped into memory more strongly, because your brain flags them as important.

scenes.headline: ONCE USEFUL
scenes.text: One idea is that remembering mistakes once helped us avoid danger.

scenes.headline: SO WHY?
scenes.text: So why do you remember embarrassing moments forever? Maybe your brain is just trying to keep you safe.
